summary: A lease renewal's saved response now expires an hour after it completes, not when its run ends. Until now a live run's in-use rule kept every renewal's receipt, about 3.3 KB of step view each, for as long as the run lasted. Measured on a copy of a real member, the first pass gave back 0.79% of the file, about 4.4 KB per expired receipt, and cut response-receipt storage by 80%.

replay.detail: No replay and no scan at open. The response-expiry task runs a second pass in its own writer transactions. It walks idempotency by rowid from a cursor in meta, 64 rows or 20 ms per transaction with 20 ms between, as the existing cleanup does. Published receipts on the way are passed over and left to the 7-day cleanup.

schema.detail: One meta key is added: idempotency_replay_safe_through, the pass's cursor. No table, column, index, trigger, kind, digest or storage version changes.

rules.detail: Replay-safe receipts older than [trim] replay_safe_receipts are deleted. The default is 1h; 0, or any window of 7 days or more, keeps the 7-day rule. The runtime decides what stays: a renewal's step view goes whatever state its run is in, because a renewal retried after its receipt is gone renews again, or is refused as any renewal is once the lease has ended. It never gets idempotency-key-expired. A run or revision apply receipt is also replay-safe, but it keeps the in-use rule and is left in place for the 7-day cleanup. Published receipts keep 7 days. The client contract (docs/st3/client-v0) says renewals last an hour. Slimming the renewal receipt itself (storing less than the whole step view) is not done: at an hour's retention these receipts hold about 1/168 of what they held, and slimming would change what a retried renewal returns.

compatibility.detail: Receipts are host-local, never replicated, digested or advertised, so peers of any version are unaffected in both directions. Measured: the replication inventory digest was equal before and after the pass. The new config key is optional and its default is not written. A config that sets it is refused by an older build, as any unknown [trim] key is.

downtime.detail: No downtime. Measured on a copy of the member: 99.95% of its replay-safe receipts went in 2,230 writer transactions, p50 8.7 ms, p99 31 ms, max 45 ms. The freed pages went back at 128 per write: p50 8.1 ms, p99 31 ms, max 47 ms. No write reached 100 ms.

manual.detail: Nothing to do. To keep renewals' receipts longer, set [trim] replay_safe_receipts to a window such as "6h"; "0" keeps them the full 7 days. A store without incremental auto-vacuum reuses the freed pages but does not shrink (see docs/st3/retention.md).

recovery.detail: Rolling back to the previous release is supported. Remove [trim] replay_safe_receipts first if you set it, because the previous release refuses an unknown key. The previous release ignores the cursor and goes back to the 7-day rule with the in-use pin. Receipts this release deleted stay deleted, and a renewal retried against one renews again.
